name: OpenAPI Definition Builder
description: Build an OpenAPI 3.2 definition builder that treats OpenAPI documents as build artifacts generated from canonical definition fragments using kind:scope/domain/name identities, target-local naming, collision reports, and migration from the current domain merge path.

userStories.title: Define canonical ID grammar and parser
userStories.description: As a schema author, I want every OpenAPI fragment to use a fixed canonical identity so that definitions can be referenced independently from output component names.
acceptanceCriteria: Define canonical ID grammar as kind:scope/domain/name.
Supported kind values include schema, response, parameter, requestBody, header, link, callback, path, operation, server, tag, and securityScheme.
Scope represents API exposure or server family such as shared, public, admin, internal, or partner.
Domain represents bounded context such as common, book, notebook, auth, user, or health.
Name is the domain-local definition name and should be PascalCase for component-like definitions.
Reject malformed IDs such as schema:book/Note and schema:Note.
Reject nested IDs such as schema:public/book/chapter/Note.
Add fixtures for schema:public/book/Note, schema:public/notebook/Note, and schema:shared/common/Error.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with canonical ID grammar and examples.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: This story is the foundation. Keep it small: grammar, parser/validator, fixtures, docs. Do not implement bundle emit here.

userStories.title: Add fragment definition model
userStories.description: As a builder developer, I want a definition node model so that each fragment can carry source metadata, references, and content hash.
acceptanceCriteria: Define DefinitionNode with canonical ID, kind, scope, domain, local name, source path, source pointer, content hash, metadata, and refs.
Define DefinitionRef for source refs found inside fragment content.
Preserve source path and pointer for diagnostics.
Include optional metadata for classification that does not belong in canonical ID hierarchy.
Tests cover definition node construction and source metadata preservation.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with the definition node model if the public architecture changes.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: Depends on canonical ID grammar. Keep this as data model and tests only.

userStories.title: Build definition registry graph
userStories.description: As a builder, I want to load fragments into a registry graph so that refs, duplicates, and target bundles can be analyzed before OpenAPI emission.
acceptanceCriteria: Add registry data structures for definition nodes and ref edges.
Collect refs using JSON Pointer-aware traversal.
Detect duplicate canonical IDs as errors.
Preserve source coordinates for every diagnostic where possible.
Tests cover node registration, ref edge collection, and duplicate canonical ID rejection.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with registry behavior if architecture details change.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: Registry graph should not emit OpenAPI yet. It should only model nodes, refs, and diagnostics.

userStories.title: Resolve canonical and file refs
userStories.description: As a schema author, I want source refs to use canonical identity syntax so that fragments can reference concepts rather than emitted OpenAPI names.
acceptanceCriteria: Support canonical refs such as oa://schema/public/book/Note.
Support relative file refs where feasible and normalize them to canonical IDs.
Preserve unsupported or missing ref diagnostics.
Tests cover canonical ref, file ref, missing ref, unsupported ref, and nested ref resolution.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with canonical ref syntax.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: Reuse existing parser/source/ref traversal primitives where possible.

userStories.title: Rewrite output OpenAPI refs
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want source refs rewritten into valid OpenAPI $ref strings so that emitted documents are standard OpenAPI 3.2.
acceptanceCriteria: Rewrite request body, header, link, callback, and security scheme refs to their correct OpenAPI component locations.
Emit only standard OpenAPI $ref values in final documents.
Tests verify output refs contain no oa:// refs.
Update docs/internal/spec.md if ref rewrite behavior changes.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: Can be implemented before full document emit as a pure rewrite helper over registry nodes.

userStories.title: Implement target-local naming policies
userStories.description: As an API owner, I want output component names to be deterministic within each target so that public, admin, and internal bundles can resolve names independently.
acceptanceCriteria: Same canonical ID included in different targets may produce the same output name without cross-target leakage.
If local names collide in one target, output names use domain prefix, such as BookNote and NotebookNote.
Emit alias metadata mapping canonical ID to output name and policy reason.
Tests cover unique names, same local name across domains, and same canonical ID across different targets.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with naming policy details.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: This is target-local output naming only. It must not change canonical IDs.

userStories.title: Simulate server and domain name collisions
userStories.description: As a schema platform maintainer, I want collision behavior simulated across server targets and domains so that naming policy is proven before replacing current merge output.
acceptanceCriteria: Add fixture target public-api including schema:public/book/Note and schema:public/notebook/Note.
Add fixture target admin-api including schema:admin/book/Note and another colliding local name.
Verify same local name across domains emits deterministic output names.
Verify same local name across targets remains target-local.
Emit a machine-readable collision report with canonical ID, target name, scope, domain, local name, output name, reason, and severity.
Tests cover no collision, rename collision, and target-local naming.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with collision report shape.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: PRD review addition: simulate target server > domain > local name behavior explicitly.

userStories.title: Simulate path flattening collision risks
userStories.description: As a schema platform maintainer, I want path-aware canonical identities tested against flattened output names so that schema:public/a/Name and schema:public/aname/Name are not treated as the same definition.
acceptanceCriteria: Add fixtures for schema:public/a/Name, schema:public/aname/Name, schema:public/a-name/Name, and schema:admin/a/Name.
Verify all fixtures have distinct canonical identities.
Run naming policy simulation and detect flattened output symbol collisions.
Emit output-name-collision when multiple canonical IDs map to the same attempted output name.
Collision diagnostics include all colliding canonical IDs and attempted output name.
Builder either renames deterministically or fails according to target policy.
Tests prove no semantic dedupe occurs only because flattened names match.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with flattening guard behavior.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: Canonical identity and output symbol equivalence must never be inferred by string flattening.

userStories.title: Define duplicate and dedupe policy
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want explicit duplicate and dedupe rules so that structural similarity does not collapse semantically different definitions.
acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate canonical ID is an error.
Duplicate output name is handled by naming policy or explicit alias.
Identical schema hash across different canonical IDs produces warning/info only by default.
No automatic structural dedupe occurs unless explicit semantic alias/ref is declared.
Tests cover identical shape but different meaning remaining separate.
Tests cover explicit semantic alias as the only allowed dedupe path.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with duplicate and dedupe policy.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: Keep structural dedupe opt-in through explicit semantic aliasing.

userStories.title: Add target bundle configuration
userStories.description: As an API owner, I want target configs for public, admin, and internal APIs so that only selected scopes, domains, servers, and paths are emitted.
acceptanceCriteria: Define target config format with name, scopes, domains, servers, include paths, and naming policy.
Target can include shared plus target-specific scopes.
Target selection includes directly matched paths.
Target selection recursively includes referenced schemas, parameters, responses, and other components.
Tests cover public versus admin target selection.
Tests cover target-local output name allocation.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with target config format.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: Target selection should be implemented before full OpenAPI emit.

userStories.title: Emit OpenAPI 3.2 document from registry
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want the builder to emit a valid OpenAPI 3.2 document from selected fragments so that current merge output can eventually be replaced.
acceptanceCriteria: Emit root openapi, info, servers, paths, webhooks, and components.
Preserve OAS 3.2 fields such as dataValue, serializedValue, and itemSchema.
Add fixture target that emits book and notebook APIs with colliding Note source names.
Output includes alias metadata or sidecar report for renamed definitions.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with emitted output behavior.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: Do not replace current .merged.yaml in this story.

userStories.title: Add CLI entry for definition builder
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want a build command for target OpenAPI documents so that the builder can run locally and in CI.
acceptanceCriteria: Add CLI command or script such as oa-gen build-spec --target ... .
Exit non-zero on duplicate canonical ID or unresolved required refs.
Tests cover success and failure CLI cases.
Update docs/internal/api-index.md if public exports change.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: CLI likely belongs in @oa-sdk/codegen while fixtures/layout remain in @oa-sdk/schemas.

userStories.title: Integrate builder metadata with WorkspaceIndex
userStories.description: As a user of large specs, I want fragment-level changes to dirty only affected target bundles so that multi-server schema builds can become incremental.
acceptanceCriteria: Store fragment file/hash/id/ref metadata in WorkspaceIndex or adjacent builder index.
Changing a schema fragment dirties target bundles that include it directly or transitively.
Changing target config dirties only that target.
Driver fallback and full rebuild principles match ADR-006.
Tests cover changed schema fragment invalidating dependent target.
Initial implementation may use full rebuild while storing enough metadata for later incremental optimization.
Update docs/internal/spec.md with builder index metadata.
Update docs/internal/todo.md with story completion or follow-up status.
userStories.notes: This can be metadata-only first. Do not require optimized rebuild to be perfect before builder correctness is proven.

userStories.title: Document migration from current domain merge
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a migration plan from current domain-level merge.ts to the definition builder so that current schemas remain stable during transition.
acceptanceCriteria: Document current merge path and new builder path side by side.
Define which current files become fragments.
Include rollback plan: current merge remains available until builder output matches expected validation.
Document when builder output can replace .merged.yaml.
Update tasks/prd-openapi-definition-builder.md if migration story changes.
userStories.notes: Final documentation and migration story. Keep current packages/schemas/scripts/merge.ts available.
